Faster storage for the PS Vita (HENkaku/Ensō, firmware 3.60–3.74). A fork of [Vita Turbo Storage](https://github.com/juanjsebgarcia/vita-turbo-storage) by Juan Garcia Alvite.

Makes a microSD in an SD2Vita, the Sony memory card and the internal storage read and write faster. The system's driver is not modified, what you read and write is byte-for-byte the same, writes are never cached or delayed, and any error switches that storage back to the standard path.

### Speed (my console, microSD in an SD2Vita, 1 MiB reads into ordinary memory)

| Without plugin | GPU-safe reads off | GPU-safe reads on (default) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 13.5 MiB/s | **19.6 MiB/s** | **18.3 MiB/s** |

What the reading costs the game's own CPU core, per MiB read (GPU-safe reads on): about 22 ms with the copy on the game's core, about **3 ms** with *Copy on the system core* (the default).

**In games.** The gain is smaller than in a file copy, because most of a game's loading time is not storage. It is still there when a game loads data into ordinary (cached) memory: those reads get the same speed-up as above. Reads into non-cacheable memory (what a game sets aside for data the graphics chip reads) are left exactly as the system does them: same speed, no change. A game can do both in one session; the plugin decides per read, from the buffer.

### New in 1.1.0

- **Even less work on the game's core:** with *Copy on the system core*, the game's thread no longer prepares the access to its buffer itself; that moved to the system core too. On my console the game's core now spends about 3 ms per MiB read instead of 4 (about 22 ms without *Copy on the system core*). The reading speed is unchanged.
- **Tester:** a core meter shows how busy each game core (0, 1, 2) really was during the reads and writes. It replaces the per-thread CPU time of 1.0, which counted part of the time a read waits for the card as work. The 1.0 notes said "7 instead of 27 ms"; measured with the core meter it is 4 instead of 22 ms (3 now).
- **Tester:** non-cacheable reads also into physically contiguous memory and into CDRAM, as games keep graphics data.

### New in 1.0.0

- **Copy on the system core is on by default** (*GPU-safe only*) and no longer experimental. While a game loads, its own CPU core does a fraction of the work it did before; the reading speed is about the same (1–2% less). **Updating from 0.7 or 0.8:** your saved setting is kept, so if it says *Off*, set it to *GPU-safe only* in Settings > Devices > vita-memio > Advanced.
- **Tester:** the exact build of the tester and of the plugin running on the console.
- Less CPU work per read when planning overlapped reads.
- The log names the exact build at every start.

### New in 0.8.0 (bug fixes)

- **More robust when several things happen at once:** settings changed while a game reads, two storages read at the same time, statistics read meanwhile. Every value shared between threads is now read and written as a whole, and settings are applied one change at a time.
- **Copy on the system core** checks the game's buffer more carefully before using it, and once it has refused a buffer type it does not change its mind halfway.
- **A stuck card no longer holds up the plugin:** if a read hangs in the system driver (for example a card pulled out mid-read), switching overlapped reads off no longer waits for it forever; the plugin retries a moment later.
- The tester's report says whether GPU-safe reads were on.

### New in 0.7.0

- **Small reads faster with GPU-safe reads:** about 5% more on reads of 32–64 KiB. Without GPU-safe reads they stay as fast as before.
- **Steadier while a game keeps the CPU busy:** the card goes from one part of a read to the next by itself, instead of waiting for the game's thread to come back.
- **Copy on the system core** (new; Settings > Devices > vita-memio > Advanced): copies what a game or app reads on the console's spare core instead of its own, so that core is free sooner while it loads. *GPU-safe only* or *Always*. Applies to reads of 64 KiB or more into ordinary memory. The reading speed stays about the same (1–2% less in the tester); it only moves the work. If the console does not allow it, reads are copied as before.
- The plugin's own background work runs on the system core and only wakes up when there is something to do.
- The log (when enabled) says more about what the plugin is doing, in shorter lines.

### New in 0.6.x

- **Overlapped reads** (*Off*, *Auto*, *Fixed*) and **GPU-safe reads**, both on by default.
- Games that load a lot of graphics data no longer lose speed with the plugin on: those reads go into non-cacheable memory and are left to the system.
- Settings can be changed in safe mode; a start only counts as good after 30 seconds on the home screen.
- New logo, tester icon and LiveArea.

### Install

1. Copy `vitamemio_kernel.skprx` and `vitamemio.suprx` to `ur0:tai/` (always both).
2. In your taiHEN config, add `ur0:tai/vitamemio_kernel.skprx` under `*KERNEL` and `ur0:tai/vitamemio.suprx` under `*NPXS10015`. If `ux0:tai/config.txt` exists, edit that one: it is read first.
3. Restart, then switch your storage on in **Settings > Devices > vita-memio**.
4. Optional: install `vitamemio_tester.vpk` with VitaShell.

Suggested for playing: just switch your storage on; the defaults are the recommended settings. Holding **L** at start-up skips all plugins.

Tested on one console (PCH-1000, firmware 3.65). Use at your own risk and keep a backup of your cards.

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of the files.
